s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of unilateral weakness and vomiting with a history of transient neurological symptoms
salient_findings: Right ankle clonus and upgoing plantar response
key_facts: 36-year-old man of Indian origin
Presented at 2:30 a.m. with acute symptoms
Awoke around midnight with headache and vomiting
No visual change or speech disturbance
History of odd sensations and occasional tremors in right arm and leg
No medical history
Nonsmoker, denied alcohol or drug use
Normal vital signs
Normal cardiorespiratory examination
Incidental 4 × 6 mm hyperdense focus in left parasagittal frontal cortex on CT
Normal CT angiography and CT perfusion
Normal laboratory studies except for total protein of 87 g/L
Normal chest radiograph, ECG, and transthoracic echocardiography
Recent ischemic infarction in left paramedian medulla on MRI

shortlist.label: Ischemic stroke
shortlist.why_kept: Recent ischemic infarction in left paramedian medulla on MRI

shortlist.label: Cerebral vasculitis
shortlist.why_kept: Acute onset of unilateral weakness and vomiting with a history of transient neurological symptoms

shortlist.label: Reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: History of headache and vomiting, with normal CT angiography and CT perfusion

shortlist.label: Cavernous malformation
shortlist.why_kept: Incidental 4 × 6 mm hyperdense focus in left parasagittal frontal cortex on CT, suggestive of a cavernoma

shortlist.label: Central nervous system vasculitis
shortlist.why_kept: Acute onset of unilateral weakness and vomiting, with a history of odd sensations and occasional tremors in right arm and leg

raw.rationale: The patient presented with acute right-sided weakness and vomiting, and brain MRI showed a recent ischemic infarction in the left paramedian medulla, which explains the key facts without contradiction.

rejected.label: Cerebral vasculitis
rejected.why: There is no evidence of inflammation or vasculitis on laboratory studies or imaging.

rejected.label: Reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings do not suggest reversible vasoconstriction.

rejected.label: Cavernous malformation
rejected.why: Although the patient has a small frontal cavernoma, it is not likely the cause of the acute symptoms and ischemic infarction in the medulla.

rejected.label: Central nervous system vasculitis
rejected.why: There is no evidence of systemic vasculitis or inflammation, and the imaging findings are more consistent with an ischemic stroke.
